# Enclii LLM Context Pointer

Generated: 2026-05-29

## Purpose

This pointer file gives LLM agents a stable, tool-agnostic map for working in this
repository without depending on vendor-specific instruction files.

## Canonical instruction order

1. `AGENTS.md`
2. `README.md` if present
3. `ECOSYSTEM.md` if present
4. Relevant files under `docs/`, `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, and source
   directories for the specific task

## Agent compatibility

`AGENTS.md` is the source of truth. `CLAUDE.md` exists only to redirect Claude
and other legacy agent integrations to `AGENTS.md`.

## Enclii-first operations contract

Use Enclii web, API, or CLI for routine production provisioning, deployment,
observability, domain management, secrets, provider operations, scaling,
rollback, and remediation.

Raw `kubectl`, `helm`, SSH, provider CLIs/APIs, `docker exec`, and direct
container access are allowed only for platform bootstrap or documented
break-glass emergencies when Enclii is unavailable or lacks an implemented
adapter. Any break-glass use must record the actor, reason, target
service/environment, commands executed, result, and follow-up Enclii adapter
gap or incident link.

## Recent operating-contract changes (2026-08-27)

Three behaviors changed on this date; agents carrying older context will be
wrong about all three. (1) One-off job dispatch resolves Deployments by
`<name>` / `<name>-web` / `<namespace>-web` and turns deterministic admission
denials into a terminal `failed` status with `failure_reason` persisted — see
`docs/cli/commands/jobs.md`. (2) Tunnel-route writes are guarded: backends must
resolve to a live Service+port, changed rules are canaried and reverted on
dial failure, and manifest capture refuses domains declared under a Service-doc
name with no live workload (the 2026-08-27 identity-outage class). (3) The
reusable `build-publish.yml` (v1.0.0-alpha.5) derives digests from the
registry, not Actions artifacts, and its guard requires pins_written > 0.

## DNS, domains and CLI identity (2026-09-07)

Learned during a live tenant onboarding; an agent carrying older context will be
wrong about all of it.

- DNS records (`providers cloudflare dns-apply`), fixed in #536: for
  **TXT/MX/NS/SRV** a record's identity includes its **content**, so several
  records coexist at one name. Same name+type+content -> `noop`; different
  content -> `create`, leaving the existing records alone; `--replace` (literal
  "true") is the explicit way to overwrite one, and it warns about both the
  value it destroys and the siblings it leaves. CNAME/A/AAAA keep single-record
  update semantics. The dry-run plan is what the apply executes — both decide
  from one live read via one function. Do NOT reach for the Cloudflare
  dashboard to add a second TXT or MX; any runbook step saying so predates
  #536. Before it, a record was keyed by name+type only and a second TXT/MX was
  applied as a destructive `update` of the first (issue #530, hit live on
  2026-09-07: an SPF TXT destroyed a Proton ownership TXT).
- MX priority is a first-class `--priority` flag (#536). The old form — the
  preference inside `--content` as `"10 mail.example.com"` — still works and is
  split back out server-side; the flag wins when both are given, and the
  response reports `priority_source`. A create with no priority defaults to 10
  and says so; a non-numeric or out-of-range value is `invalid_request`, not a
  silent default; priority 0 is legal and preserved. The old `--type MX --apply`
  502 was this: the MX create carried no `priority` field at all, Cloudflare
  answered 400, and every provider error below the handler was rendered 502. A
  record Cloudflare refuses is now 422 (409 duplicate, 424 zone/credential,
  400 bad argument) carrying Cloudflare's own message; 502 is reserved for a
  genuinely unreachable provider, and still does not say whether the write
  landed — re-read the zone before retrying.
- Brand-host onboarding order (verified 2026-09-07): `domains add` **from the
  repo root** (the `-f` parser validates `spec.build.dockerfile` against
  `os.Getwd()`, not the manifest's directory) -> `dns-apply` proxied CNAME ->
  `tunnels-apply` dry run (plan must show only a create for the new host) -> `dns-apply`
  the verification TXT -> `domains verify`. Then `zone-settings-apply` once the
  zone is active (`always_use_https`, `automatic_https_rewrites`,
  `min_tls_version=1.2`; verify `curl -sSI http://<host>/` -> 301). A
  manifest-only merge builds nothing, so no capture runs and a newly declared
  host does not become live. Full runbook:
  `docs/runbooks/DOMAIN_AND_EMAIL_DNS_ONBOARDING.md`.
- `tunnels-apply` derives each backend from the junction's service AND
  environment (`junctions.environment_id`, else the domain record's
  environment, else production; non-production never falls back to the
  production namespace). An UPDATE that changes the service or namespace of a
  hostname whose live backend is serving, or moves a route between production
  and another environment, is `REPOINT (blocked)`; the summary leads with
  `REFUSED` and the apply writes nothing while any row is blocked.
  `--allow-repoint <host>` is per hostname; `--expect-plan <fp>` pins the
  reviewed plan. Wrong bindings are fixed with `enclii ops junctions rebind`
  (dry run by default, data only). The automated reconcile paths refuse the
  same repoints. Operator procedure (CLI `v1.0.0-alpha.14`, released
  2026-10-02, carries `--allow-repoint`, `--expect-plan` and
  `ops junctions rebind`):
  1. dry run;
  2. review every row (label, `reason`, `environment_source`);
  3. apply with `--expect-plan` bound to the reviewed plan;
  4. when a project's hostnames are served by more than one service or
     environment, rebind the junctions first, then start again at step 1.
  The dry run and the apply are separate steps with a review between them;
  never run or paste them as one block. Procedure:
  `docs/cli/commands/providers.md#cloudflare-tunnels-apply-operator-procedure`.
  Runbook: `docs/runbooks/ENCLII_JUNCTION_ROUTE_RECONCILIATION_2026-05-16.md`.
- After a nameserver switch, clients on a stale resolver see NXDOMAIN for hosts
  that exist only in the new zone (and Cloudflare 1034 for a DNS-only host the
  old zone pointed at a CDN) for up to the old NS TTL. Do not cut over
  redirects, and do not "fix" a record that already reads correctly at the
  zone's own nameservers, until public resolvers agree.
- CLI: `enclii whoami`/`login`/`logout`/`version` print on **stderr** (cobra
  `cmd.Println` -> `OutOrStderr()`; the CLI never calls `SetOut`), so
  `whoami > file` captures nothing. A plain `enclii login` resolves whichever
  Janua identity the browser session holds. Since `v1.0.0-alpha.10` (#612),
  `--prompt select_account|login` chooses the account, and `--profile NAME`
  (or `ENCLII_PROFILE`) keeps each identity's login in its own file
  (`~/.enclii/profiles/NAME/credentials.json`; the default profile stays at
  `~/.enclii/credentials.json`). `enclii --profile admin login --no-browser
  --prompt login` plus a private window holds an operator identity without
  touching the browser's session.
  Check the binary with `enclii version 2>&1`. `v1.0.0-alpha.9` (2026-09-08)
  was the first release with `--tenant` / `providers porkbun ping` (#527) and
  `dns-apply --priority` plus the non-destructive multi-record fix (#536);
  `v1.0.0-alpha.10` adds profiles and the `provision oidc` redirect reconcile
  (#561). An alpha.8 `dns-apply` still keys TXT/MX by name+type and will
  destructively overwrite a sibling record that the current runbook says is
  safe to add.
- Per-tenant Porkbun (#527): merging does NOT apply the Vault policy. Run
  `scripts/apply-switchyard-vault-policy-remote.sh` (token on stdin, never
  argv) before the first `--tenant` call, or it 403s and reads as "credentials
  missing". Recipe: `docs/infrastructure/porkbun-tenant-credentials.md`.
- ExternalSecrets under `infra/k8s/base/external-secrets/vault-secrets/` are
  **excluded from ArgoCD**: the `external-secrets-config` Application syncs a
  five-entry `directory.include` allowlist, so a merged change to any of the 19
  per-app manifests is a **silent no-op** — no OutOfSync, no drift alert, no CI
  failure. #535 (a `CTM_RESEND_API_KEY` key on `janua-secrets.yaml`) merged
  green and never reached the cluster; it was applied by a raw JSON patch on the
  live object. #634 (`resend-webhook-secret-ctm`, 2026-09-26) repeated it. The
  directory is also non-recursive, and the live objects were bootstrapped by
  `scripts/cluster-ops-deploy.sh` (client-side `kubectl apply`). Issue #539
  tracks the sanctioned path (`enclii secrets es-apply`, or
  reconcile-then-include). Do NOT assume merging a `vault-secrets/*.yaml`
  change deploys it: patch the live object additively AND keep git in step
  (procedure in `docs/infrastructure/EXTERNAL_SECRETS.md`).
- `enclii ops secrets sync|refresh` only patches ExternalSecret annotations
  (`force-sync` + `enclii.dev/*`); it never touches values or `spec`.
  `enclii ops pods restart` is NOT implemented: apply returns HTTP 501
  `adapter_required` (dry-run looks fine). Roll the Deployment via
  `POST /v1/services/{id}/restart` (registered services) or break-glass
  rollout restart. Doc: `docs/cli/commands/ops.md`.
- ExternalSecret ordering: **Vault property first, manifest second.** An
  ExternalSecret is all-or-nothing — one missing property fails the whole sync
  and the target Secret keeps its old data, or on a first sync is never created.
  Use `vault kv patch` when the path exists and `vault kv put` when it does not:
  KV v2 answers **404** to a patch on a never-written path. #529 retired the
  committed Verdaccio Secret in the same change that introduced its
  ExternalSecret replacement, so ArgoCD pruned the old value before the Vault
  key existed (fixed in #534).
- Reloader reads `reloader.stakater.com/auto` on the **Deployment's own
  `metadata.annotations`**, never on the pod template. An annotation on the
  template is silently inert — Verdaccio carried one there since 2026-05 and it
  never fired, so a rotated htpasswd left the pod serving the kubelet's stale
  projection while reporting `Ready` (#534).
- npm.madfam.io credentials do not mix: a **Janua API key** (`jnk_…`) goes in
  `_auth` (HTTP Basic) and NEVER in `_authToken` — `security.api.jwt` makes
  Verdaccio verify a Bearer token as its own JWT before any plugin runs, and the
  failure degrades to *anonymous* rather than 401, so the key is never seen. An
  **htpasswd password** (e.g. the rotated admin) uses
  `npm login --auth-type=legacy` (without it npm tries a web login flow this
  registry does not serve). The **CI service token** is a Verdaccio-issued JWT
  and does belong in `_authToken`. htpasswd itself is Vault-sourced
  (`secret/npm-registry #htpasswd` -> ExternalSecret `verdaccio-auth`), never
  committed; rotate one-shot with
  `scripts/operator/npm-registry-admin-password-rotate.sh`. Doc:
  `docs/infrastructure/npm-registry.md`.
- Cloudflare **Redirect Rules** have no Enclii op (issue #538). The 2026-09-07
  brand-migration 301s (`crea-map.madfam.io` -> `map.creatumundo.mx`,
  `crea-erp` -> `erp`) were created in the dashboard as documented break-glass.
  The source host must keep a **proxied** DNS record or the rule never fires.
  Break-glass procedure: `docs/runbooks/DOMAIN_AND_EMAIL_DNS_ONBOARDING.md`.


## Next.js images and the runner npm removal (2026-09-30)

Every Next app is on **16.3.8**
(GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j, `next/og` RCE; `apps/admin-console/app/icon.tsx` uses
`ImageResponse`). `apps/status` installs from its OWN
`apps/status/pnpm-lock.yaml` with `--frozen-lockfile`: a Next bump that
regenerates only the root lockfile breaks the status image build (#659 ->
#660). The runner stage of `status`, `dispatch` and `switchyard-ui` deletes
`npm`/`npx` (Trivy HIGHs lived only in npm's vendored tree, and the runtimes
only run `node server.js`); do not "fix" a runner by calling npm, and do not
drop the deletion. CI job `runner-npm-lint` (`scripts/check-runner-no-npm.py`)
enforces it and documents how to add npm back. Baseline: `README.md` ->
"Security".

## CI contracts (2026-10-01/02)

- GitHub-hosted runners are pinned to `ubuntu-24.04` ahead of GitHub moving
  `ubuntu-latest` to Ubuntu 26 on 2026-10-19 (#662). Doc examples use the pin.
- `arc-runner-image.yml` pushes every build by its sha tag and moves `:stable`
  only after both smoke checks and the cosign signature; pull requests never
  push (#664). Pinned by `tests/scripts/test_arc_runner_image_promotion.py`.
- `weighbridge.yml` and `deploy-pipeline-monitor.yml` commit their own digest
  pin and race other pins on the same push. A rejected push retries up to 5
  times: fetch, reset onto `origin/main`, re-apply the digest, exit 0 when
  fresh main already pins it (#665). `tests/scripts/test_digest_pin_push_retry.py`
  runs the step's script verbatim against a throwaway bare origin. Both run in
  the `workflow-contracts` job of `ci.yml`.
- `packages/sdk-py` models are generated from `docs/api/openapi.yaml` with
  `datamodel-code-generator==0.83.0` (exact pin, no committed lockfile);
  `sdk-py.yml` triggers on the spec paths and fails on drift (#663).
- Skipped tests and known flakes: `docs/testing/SKIPPED_TESTS.md`.
